title: Wrangler-seam probe drives two concurrent increments against the DO through env.CELL and one WebSocket upgrade through env.HUB, both routed via the DO facade so the sole-reader guarantee holds
asA: reviewer verifying the platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0 blueprint under a real workerd runtime
iWant: the wrangler-seam probe to spawn wrangler dev on the cf-platform fixture, issue two concurrent POST /cell/<id>/increment requests against a route in src/index.mjs that reaches env.CELL through the DO facade (createDoFacade({env}).cellFetch), and open one WebSocket upgrade against /hub/<id>/connect that reaches env.HUB through the facade (createDoFacade({env}).hubFetch), asserting per-instance serialisation on the increments and one broadcast frame on the WebSocket
soThat: the shipped DO facade + SingleCellObject + HubObject code path is proven against workerd, not only against the in-memory storage driver and the fake websocket state that the six in-process probes drive

acceptanceCriteria.description: The wrangler-seam probe, when the fixture has been prepared with `pnpm install --ignore-workspace` so the wrangler devDependency is on the tree, spawns `wrangler dev --local --port 0` from the cf-platform fixture, waits bounded 45 seconds for the CLI to bind, then (a) issues two concurrent POST /cell/<id>/increment requests against a fetch route in src/index.mjs that calls createDoFacade({env, sink}).cellFetch(<id>, request), asserting the two responses observe per-instance serialisation (sorted counters == [1, 2], sorted witnesses == [0, 1], each request read the other's write) and (b) opens one WebSocket upgrade against /hub/<id>/connect via createDoFacade({env, sink}).hubFetch(<id>, request), asserting one broadcast frame arrives on connect with payload 'hello-from-hub'. The probe kills wrangler cleanly on exit. Warn semantics per section 3.1 pass-with-skip: if wrangler is not installed or fails to bind within the cap, the probe returns aggregateVerdict warn (never fail); a handler thrown at the workerd boundary is a genuine fail. The additional result on the same probe run covers AC-33108-1 by grepping the fixture wrangler.toml for the two [[durable_objects.bindings]] pairs and the [[migrations]] tag/new_sqlite_classes pair; the grep result is deterministic and does not require wrangler.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the cf-platform fixture with the wrangler devDependency installed and the shipped DO classes exported from src/index.mjs
acceptanceCriteria.then: wrangler dev binds; two concurrent increments through env.CELL observe per-instance serialisation; one WebSocket upgrade through env.HUB receives a broadcast frame; the wrangler.toml grep confirms both binding pairs and the migrations tag/new_sqlite_classes; wrangler exits cleanly

acceptanceCriteria.description: Wrangler-not-installed warn: if pnpm install --ignore-workspace has not been run under the cf-platform fixture and the wrangler bin is not on the fixture's node_modules/.bin, the wrangler-seam probe returns aggregateVerdict:"warn" naming DO_WRANGLER_NOT_INSTALLED with the expected bin path. This is a genuine "cannot verify" state, not a runtime defect (warn semantics per section 3.1 pass-with-skip).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a cf-platform fixture whose node_modules does not contain wrangler

acceptanceCriteria.description: Bind-timeout warn: if wrangler dev --local --port 0 does not bind within the 45-second cap, the probe returns aggregateVerdict:"warn" naming DO_WRANGLER_BIND_TIMEOUT with the observed stderr quoted. The probe kills the wrangler child on the timeout.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a probe run where wrangler cannot bind within 45 seconds (simulated by an environment that blocks its listen)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the probe caps the wait at 45 seconds
acceptanceCriteria.then: aggregateVerdict is "warn" naming DO_WRANGLER_BIND_TIMEOUT with the observed stderr

acceptanceCriteria.description: Workerd handler thrown = fail (not warn): if wrangler binds but a request through env.CELL or env.HUB throws inside the workerd runtime (e.g. the DO handler rejects with an uncaught error), the probe returns aggregateVerdict:"fail" naming DO_WORKERD_HANDLER_THREW with the observed response body. A handler thrown is a genuine runtime defect, distinct from the warn cases above.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a probe run where a POST /cell/<id>/increment triggers a handler that throws inside workerd
acceptanceCriteria.when: the probe issues the concurrent requests

acceptanceCriteria.description: Probe teardown: the wrangler child is killed on probe exit (normal or exceptional) via SIGTERM followed by SIGKILL after a 5-second grace period. An interrupted probe still tears down within 6 seconds; no orphan wrangler process remains.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a probe run interrupted by an assertion rejection after the CLI binds
acceptanceCriteria.then: the wrangler child is terminated within 6 seconds; no orphan process remains
